blocks.content: Statutory audit is a legally mandated examination of financial statements to ensure a true and fair view of the company's financial state.

rows: Form opinion on True & Fair view of financials
Evaluate internal controls and operational efficiency

items: Section 139 of the Companies Act, 2013 regarding the appointment of statutory auditors is frequently tested in competitive exam MCQs.
Remember the distinction: Statutory Auditors report to Shareholders, whereas Internal Auditors report to Management.
Tax audit thresholds under Section 44AB and Secretarial Audit limits under Section 204 are high-yield questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Statutory audit is compulsory for all registered companies under the Companies Act, 2013.
Internal audit under Section 138 focuses on evaluating internal controls, operational efficiency, and risk management.
Tax audit under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act, 1961 is required for businesses exceeding specified turnover thresholds.
Secretarial audit under Section 204 applies to listed companies and prescribed public companies to ensure corporate law compliance.
Cost audit under Section 148 is applicable to specified companies engaged in production, processing, or manufacturing activities.
